feedback.problem:
Consider the following parabola:

$$
x=3t,\,y=\frac{3}{5}{t}^{2},\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

The Cartesian equation of the parabola is

${x}^{2}=$
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}t & =\frac{x}{3},\,{t}^{2}=\frac{5y}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the first equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=\frac{5y}{3}$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{9} & =\frac{5y}{3} \\ {x}^{2} & =15y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian equation of the parabola is ${x}^{2}=15y.$
